How long to you have to wait to see a doctor?

In the public sector like Medical, waits can approach a month, but there is usually a triage type of review available if you whine enough. In the private ACA type insurance, it depends on the type of insurance purchased, PPO or HMO and the type of doctor you want to see. Under some plans a person can just "self refer" and under others, they have to go through their "gatekeeper" primary care physician who decides if and when to get a specialist involved. Keep in mind that wait times are closely related to public satisfaction, but less closely related to outcome benefits with an effective triage system.

Can you give me an approximation for emergencies?

Emergencies are available on demand. Federal law requires hospitals to treat all persons until stable, without regard to insurance or ability to pay. This makes hospitals a health care access point of last resort especially for the uninsured. ER care is of course the most expensive and the uninsured often wind up receiving costly emergency care which would have been much more cheaply handled in a non-emergency room setting but the ER Doc just won't take the chance that the patient isn't "stable". This make the waiting lobbies in urban hospitals located near areas of poverty highly congested with waits that are regularly 6-8 hours during peak times. These peaks often coincide with times which are counter intuitive and hard to predict. I call them the Friday and Saturday night "knife and gun" club.
